Issue Details
### Description I am embadding monovm, I write a function `mono_alc_load_assembly_with_partial_name` extend from `mono_assembly_load_with_partial_name` with `alc` argument when call `mono_image_open_from_data_alc` to load `MonoImage` the `mono_alc_from_gchandle` get the wrong `MonoAssemblyLoadContext` value ### Reproduction Steps 1 ### Expected behavior work correctly ### Actual behavior crash ### Regression? _No response_ ### Known Workarounds _No response_ ### Configuration build the latest version of release/6.0 branch x64 windows desktop ### Other information no

I found out the problem.
this is because MonoManagedAssemblyLoadContext layout is wrong with Managed `AssemblyLoadContext` https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ff82b6dde9367df1c9eb40d362e701e2d54213a2/src/mono/mono/metadata/object-internals.h#L1413

you can see the coreclr implemented:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/74f238de0e96c072b9a6e496d466cda703df2f70/src/coreclr/vm/object.h#L1477

I believe this construction is a little problematic and you see the symptoms of it. Just adding LayoutKind.Sequential might fix it, but depending on sequential field order in a partial class that is in this case not even sealed, so don't know what guarantees that will give you of complete class layout. You can also see that CoreCLR depends on a different order, that is not inline with how the fields are declared, but how they are layed out by loader. I believe a better way to fix it is to get rid of MonoManagedAssemblyLoadContext and fix mono_alc_from_gchandle to use a cached offset to the nativeAssemblyLoadContext field and then access it based on the offset instead of depending on field order in the class.

Caching the field offset is ok, but we do use `LayoutKind.Sequential` for many other partial classes in CoreLib.  It is also a reasonable approach.

> 
> Caching the field offset is ok, but we do use `LayoutKind.Sequential` for many other partial classes in CoreLib. It is also a reasonable approach.

yes, this is why I fixed it using `LayoutKind.Sequential` in my first pr.

For this class where we just depend on 1 field, it feels more deterministic to use field offset, since we will not depend on layout issues, and risk of breaking things when adding fields into any of the partial classes.
